title: OyatieKnowledgeGraphSchema
description: Canonical knowledge-graph substrate for the entire Oyatie project. Every relationship, capability, feature, schema, crate, BC, microservice, ADR, plan, lane, hook, generator, healer, owner, block — modeled as nodes + typed edges. Registries are VIEWS into this graph filtered by node_type. Single validator (oya check knowledge-graph) traverses for DRY violations, orphans, cycles, broken refs, supersession chains, ownership coverage. Hyperscaler precedent: AWS Resource Explorer + Resource Graph; GCP Asset Inventory + Cloud Asset Graph; Azure Resource Graph + Service Map; K8s API discovery + OwnerReferences; Linkerd Service Mesh topology. Per user directive 2026-05-13: 'every relationship, every capability, every feature, every schema, everything mapped graphed and tracked for automation is ideal' + 'DRY enforcement is key'.

user_directives_2026_05_13: ideally every relationship, every capability, every feature, every schema, everything mapped graphed and tracked for automation is ideal.
_meta.design_rationale: Per Torvalds-lens self-critique: registries with overlapping concerns (capabilities-registry, building-blocks-registry, lane-registry, catalog-registry) are redundant if they all model the same project state. The correct shape is ONE graph; registries are filter-views. Per AWS Resource Explorer / GCP Asset Inventory precedent at hyperscaler scale. Per decision-principles.json DP-05 (single canonical tree).
_meta.non_canonical_storage_layout_rationale: We don't ship one giant graph.json (would not scale past ~10k nodes). Instead: per-domain contributing registries each declare _contributes_node_types + _contributes_edge_types. Validator merges them at runtime. Backed by future graph-storage adapter (Neo4j, Memgraph, or Postgres with recursive CTE) when scale warrants.
_meta.purpose: Canonical knowledge-graph substrate for the entire Oyatie project. Every relationship, capability, feature, schema, crate, BC, microservice, ADR, plan, lane, hook, generator, healer, owner, block — modeled as nodes + typed edges.

node_types.description: Closed enum of allowed node types. Each contributing registry declares which it contributes.

edge_types.description: Closed enum of allowed edge types. Each edge is directional and typed.

invariants.description: Graph-level invariants the validator enforces. JSON Schema 2020-12 cannot express these alone; Rust validator implements.

contributing_registry_protocol.description: How a registry contributes to the graph. Every registry that wants to participate adds these declarations at top level.

_contributes_node_types.description: Node types this registry's rows materialize.

_contributes_edge_types.description: Edge types this registry's rows materialize.

node_extraction_path.description: JSON pointer or simple path expression (e.g., 'rows[*]') indicating where nodes are extracted from.
